plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Airy, daisy-like blooms float above feathery, thread-fine foliage. Their petals look like delicate silk, and the flowers sway in the autumn breeze, which draws butterflies and bees on warm afternoons.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through the first hard frost, often into late October in mild autumns
plants.location: Gardens across temperate North America and Europe, native to Mexico
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from the Greek word for order and harmony. Spanish priests in Mexico grew the plant in mission gardens and are said to have given it that name.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in the southern spring are washed in lavender-blue when this tree blooms. Clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers cover the canopy and then drop to carpet the pavement in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-October to November in the Southern Hemisphere, with the peak around late October
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and across Australia and parts of South America including Buenos Aires
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because it has tens of thousands of these trees. Local lore says a shower of fallen blossoms on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped lilac flowers push straight out of bare soil in damp meadows and woodland edges. The leaves are absent, so the blooms look like they have appeared by magic as other plants die back.
plants.location: Meadows and open woodland across western and central Europe, including the UK, Germany and France
plants.funFact: Despite the name it is not a true crocus. It produces colchicine, a toxic compound that plant breeders use to double chromosome numbers in crops.
